$comment: Getting to the trail, off the trail, and between stops. Hand-authored.
tools/fetch_transit.py adds precise times for the services that have an open
GTFS feed; it writes data/transit-schedules.json and never touches this file.
places  — graph nodes. Where data/route/anchors.json already has the
coordinates, reference it with `anchorId` instead of restating
them. Only places off the trail carry their own lat/lon.
`precision: stated` means the coordinate is the operator's own
published stop position, `approximate` means it was read off a map
and the page says so, because these are what a maps link uses.
operators — who runs a service, and how to reach a human.
services  — scheduled services. One service is ONE stopping pattern in ONE
direction. A shuttle where only some runs continue past the middle
of the line is two services, not one with exceptions.
walks   — a leg you cover on foot, so a journey can mix a bus with the road
walk at the end of it. Timed with the same Naismith model as the
hiking days rather than a made-up walking speed.
onDemand — taxis, private transfers and booked shared shuttles. No timetable,
so these are offered alongside the journey results, not inside them.
season is month-day only, so a pattern is not tied to one year: the trip is
in 2027 and no French or Italian summer timetable for 2027 exists yet.
Absent season means the service runs year-round.
days: "daily" or an array of weekday numbers, 0 = Sunday, matching
getUTCDay(). departures is a list of times at the FIRST stop; use frequency
instead when the service is turn-up-and-go.
confidence — how much to trust the times, and rendered in the UI:
scheduled-2027 : from a published 2027 timetable. Trust it.
pattern-2026   : the 2026 season's pattern, standing in for 2027. The
shape is right; the exact minutes will move.
estimate       : reconstructed from prose. Treat as indicative only.
gtfs — a hint for tools/fetch_transit.py, present only where an open feed
covers the service: which feed, which route (shortName and/or a longName
substring), and a `towards` substring of the trip headsign to pick the
direction. Stops are matched to `places` by proximity rather than listed,
so a feed renumbering its stop ids does not need an edit here.
Every service carries `source`, and `verifiedOn` records when a human last
looked. See docs/transit-notes.md for what must be re-checked before travel.

places.note: Trip base. Rail to Martigny and Saint-Gervais, coaches to Geneva and Courmayeur, valley buses to both trailheads.
Start of hiking day 1. Chamonix Bus line 1 runs here from town.
Navette ticket machine is beside Auberge de la Nova.
The navette stops below at Ville des Glaciers, not here.
Val Veny bus stop at the Combal dam.
Everything in Courmayeur leaves from Piazzale Monte Bianco: the valley shuttles, the tunnel coach to Chamonix, and the Aosta line.
Top of the Val Ferret shuttle and the start of walking on the shortcut day.
No road and no service. Reachable on foot only — listed so a journey can end with the walk up to it.
Where the shortcut day 7 finishes and the bus back to Chamonix starts.

places.name: Ville des Glaciers
places.note: Navette terminus in the Vallée des Glaciers. Short road walk up to Les Mottets from here.

places.name: Les Lanchettes
places.note: Parking at the head of the valley, for Refuge Robert Blanc. Only a few navettes a day come this far.

places.name: Bourg-Saint-Maurice
places.address: Gare SNCF et gare routière, Avenue de la Gare, 73700 Bourg-Saint-Maurice
places.note: TGV and TER railhead for the Beaufortain side. The Les Chapieux shuttle leaves from the coach station beside the railway station.

places.name: Notre-Dame de la Gorge
places.note: Head of the Contamines valley road, where the day 2 climb properly begins. Free village navette runs here in summer.

places.name: Saint-Gervais-les-Bains-Le Fayet
places.address: Gare SNCF, 122 Avenue de la Gare, 74190 Saint-Gervais-les-Bains
places.note: Where the Mont-Blanc Express meets the main-line trains, and the railhead for Les Contamines.

places.name: Sallanches
places.note: Main-line station with TGV connections; north end of the Y84 bus to Les Contamines.

places.name: Argentière
places.note: Mont-Blanc Express stop, and the nearest station to Le Tour.

places.name: Vallorcine
places.note: Last French stop on the Mont-Blanc Express before the Swiss border.

places.name: Le Châtelard VS
places.note: Swiss border station on the Mont-Blanc Express, and the low end of the Trient valley bus. This is Le Châtelard VS in the village; Le Châtelard-Frontière is a separate station a kilometre down the line, right on the border.

places.name: Finhaut
places.note: Mont-Blanc Express stop and one end of the Col de la Forclaz summer bus.

places.name: Col de la Forclaz
places.note: On the TMB just above Trient. Hotel here is the usual fallback when Trient is full, and it is a bus stop.

places.name: Martigny
places.address: Gare CFF, Place de la Gare, 1920 Martigny
places.note: The Swiss hub for the whole eastern half of the loop. Mont-Blanc Express to Chamonix, St-Bernard Express to Orsières, main line to Geneva, and the international coach to Aosta.

places.name: Orsières
places.note: Where you change between the Val Ferret and Champex bus lines. Train to Martigny.

places.name: Praz-de-Fort
places.note: On the day 5 valley walk, and on the La Fouly bus line.

places.name: Ferret
places.note: Highest bus stop in the Swiss Val Ferret, about 45 minutes' walk above La Fouly. Le Clou/Les Granges is a separate stop a kilometre below it, easy to mistake for this one.

places.name: Aosta
places.note: Italian rail and coach hub. The way to Courmayeur from Milan, Turin and Malpensa, and from Martigny over the Grand-Saint-Bernard.

places.name: Geneva Airport (GVA)
places.note: The usual way in. Rail station is under the terminal; transfer companies meet in the arrivals hall.

places.name: Milan Malpensa (MXP)
places.note: The Italian-side alternative, with a direct Arriva coach up the Aosta valley.

operators.name: Navettes des Chapieux (Les Arcs / Bourg-Saint-Maurice)
operators.hours: Tourist office daily 08:30–12:00 and 13:30–17:30, 13 June to 13 September
operators.note: Municipal seasonal shuttles, not a commercial line. Cash is safer than card everywhere in this valley.

operators.name: Taxi Aarthur
operators.hours: Phone booking; ring ahead rather than expecting to find one waiting
operators.note: The usual fallback for the Beaufortain side, including the long transfer round to Courmayeur when someone needs to leave the trail.

operators.name: Chamonix Mobilité (Chamonix Bus)
operators.note: Operated by Transdev for the valley. Groups over 10 can hire a bus through the commercial address above.

operators.name: SAT Mont-Blanc (Cars Région Haute-Savoie)
operators.note: Runs the Y84 between Sallanches, Saint-Gervais and Les Contamines on behalf of the region.

operators.name: Les Contamines-Montjoie free village navettes
operators.hours: Tourist office mornings 08:30–12:00; afternoons by appointment
operators.note: Free summer shuttles round the hamlets and up to Notre-Dame de la Gorge. Timetable is published on the village app each season.

operators.name: Arriva Italia — Valle d'Aosta
operators.hours: Val Ferret and Val Veny shuttles daytime only, summer season
operators.note: Runs all local transport in Courmayeur plus the commercial lines from Milan, Turin and Malpensa. Buying on board a Courmayeur shuttle carries a €4 surcharge outside the free period.

operators.name: FlixBus / BlaBlaCar Bus (Mont Blanc tunnel)
operators.hours: Roughly 06:00 to 22:30, several operators sharing the route
operators.note: The tunnel coach is sold by FlixBus, BlaBlaCar Bus, Infobus and SAVDA/Arriva under different brands on the same road. Book ahead in July; it is a small vehicle and it fills. No deeplink: FlixBus prefills a search from numeric city ids, and the only ids findable for Chamonix and Courmayeur came from a 2020 capture with nothing to confirm which city each one is. A wrong id would search between two arbitrary cities and look like it worked, so the per-service route pages are used instead.

operators.name: TMR — Transports de Martigny et Régions

deeplink.note: SBB's own deep-linking guide for business partners. Checked against the documentation, not opened in a browser — see docs/transit-notes.md.

operators.note: Runs the Mont-Blanc Express, the St-Bernard Express and the Entremont bus network. Reservation required 72 hours ahead for groups of 10 or more, and for bicycles.

operators.name: PostAuto / CarPostal Valais

deeplink.note: Same template as the other Swiss operators: the national timetable covers the PostBus whoever drives it.

operators.note: Shares the Trient valley and Forclaz stops with TMR. Everything Swiss is searchable and bookable on sbb.ch regardless of which company runs the vehicle.

operators.name: CFF / SBB — Swiss Federal Railways

deeplink.note: The one deep link in this file that fills in both ends, the date and the time. It is why the Swiss half of the trip is the easy half to book.

operators.note: The Swiss main line along Lake Geneva to Martigny. Everything Swiss is searchable on sbb.ch whoever runs the vehicle, which is why it is the booking link on most Swiss services here.

operators.name: SNCF — French national railways
operators.hours: Ticket desks at Le Fayet and Bourg-Saint-Maurice, station hours
operators.note: The Tarentaise and Mont-Blanc lines. Both journeys that touch this trip need a change and are sold as one ticket, so book through SNCF Connect rather than leg by leg.

operators.name: Mountain Drop-offs
operators.hours: 24 hours a day, every day of the year
operators.note: Door-to-door rather than a central drop point, which matters with six people and luggage. Over 20 years on this route.

operators.name: Alpybus
operators.hours: Scheduled shared departures plus private hire
operators.note: Cheaper than door-to-door because the express line uses fixed pick-up points. Three tiers: express, door-to-door, private.

services.name: Les Chapieux to Ville des Glaciers

booking.where: Ticket machine at Les Chapieux, beside Auberge de la Nova
booking.note: Cash. The machine shows how many seats are left and the first runs sell out — buy the evening before.

services.note: The road is closed to cars 07:30–18:00, which is exactly why the shuttle exists. Around 22 runs a day.

source.title: Les Arcs — Le site des Chapieux

services.name: Les Chapieux to Les Lanchettes

booking.where: Ticket machine at Les Chapieux, beside Auberge de la Nova
booking.note: Cash. Same ticket as the Ville des Glaciers runs.

services.note: Only three runs a day go beyond Ville des Glaciers to the Lanchettes parking. Everything else turns round short of it.

services.name: Bourg-Saint-Maurice to Les Chapieux

booking.where: From the driver at the Bourg-Saint-Maurice coach station
booking.note: Cash. No advance sale on this leg.

services.note: The way onto the trail if you are arriving by train rather than from Chamonix, and the way off it if someone needs to leave mid-trip.
services.caveat: Sources disagree on the departure quay at Bourg-Saint-Maurice — the resort site says Quai 7 and Refuge Robert Blanc says Quai 5. Allow time to find it.

source.title: Les Arcs — Bourg Saint Maurice to Les Chapieux

services.name: Les Chapieux to Bourg-Saint-Maurice

booking.where: From the driver at Les Chapieux

services.note: Modelled separately from the uphill runs because the return times are not a mirror of them — there is one late-morning departure and then nothing until the evening.

services.name: Chamonix Bus line 1 — Les Houches to Les Praz

booking.where: Chamonix Mobilité app, website, or a sales terminal
booking.note: Enter your Carte d'Hôte number when buying to get the discounted rate. Guest-card day passes were €5 for two days and €10 for a week in 2026.

services.note: How you get to the day 1 trailhead. Runs all year at roughly half-hourly; the summer timetable applies from 20 June.
services.caveat: The trip notes say the Carte d'Hôte makes valley buses free. The 2026 fare sheet no longer does — it gives discounted passes bought online with the card number, not free travel. Budget a few euros a head and check on arrival.

services.name: Chamonix Bus line 2 — Le Tour to Les Bossons

booking.where: Chamonix Mobilité app, website, or a sales terminal

services.note: The ride home at the end of day 7, from the Le Tour gondola station back into town.
services.caveat: The day 7 note in the itinerary says line 1 for this. On the 2026 network it is line 2 that serves Le Tour — line 1 covers the Les Houches end of the valley. Worth correcting before anyone stands at the wrong stop.

services.name: Y84 — Sallanches to Les Contamines-Montjoie

booking.where: From the driver, or through Cars Région Haute-Savoie

services.note: The road link to Les Contamines, and the way to reach the trail from a main-line station if someone joins late or leaves early.
services.caveat: The line runs all year, so no season is set, but the summer timetable only takes over in early July — in 2026 it ran from 5 July to 31 August. Frequency and fare here are indicative: the published timetable is a fixed set of runs, not a clock-face pattern. Check the SAT page before relying on a departure.

services.name: Les Contamines free navette to Notre-Dame de la Gorge

booking.where: Turn up at the stop

services.note: Saves about an hour of road walking at the start of day 2, which is the flattest and least interesting part of it.
services.caveat: Free and reliable, but the exact stops and times are only published on the village app each season, so treat the pattern as indicative.

source.title: Mairie des Contamines — navettes saisonnières gratuites

services.name: Linea Verde 924 — Courmayeur to Arp Nouvaz (Val Ferret)

booking.where: Board at Piazzale Monte Bianco
booking.note: Free during the summer period. Outside it, buying on board carries a €4 surcharge — buy at a rivendita in town instead.

services.note: The shortcut for day 4: ride to the head of the Italian Val Ferret and start walking at the foot of the Grand Col Ferret.
services.caveat: Only the 27 June to 30 August runs go all the way to Arp Nouvaz and start from Piazzale Monte Bianco; either side of that they start from Verrand and turn round lower down. Times are the 2026 shape, not a published 2027 timetable.

source.title: Arriva Italia — Courmayeur Mont Blanc summer shuttles

services.name: Linea Arancione 931 — Courmayeur to La Visaille (Val Veny)

booking.where: Board at Piazzale Monte Bianco

services.note: The other half of the day 3 shortcut: the Val Veny bus down from the Combal dam into Courmayeur.
services.caveat: Summer only, and the free period is funded by the comune one year at a time rather than guaranteed.

source.title: Arriva Italia — Courmayeur Mont Blanc summer shuttles

services.name: Mont Blanc tunnel coach — Courmayeur to Chamonix

booking.where: FlixBus, BlaBlaCar Bus or Arriva, whichever is selling that departure
booking.note: Book ahead. Fares move with demand and start around €13.

services.note: The single most useful bail-out link on the whole trip: 45 minutes under the massif from the Italian side back to base.
services.caveat: Around six to ten departures a day depending on the operator and date, and the exact times shift. The list here is a representative 2026 pattern — check the operator before counting on one.

services.name: Mont Blanc tunnel coach — Chamonix to Courmayeur

booking.where: FlixBus, BlaBlaCar Bus or Arriva

services.note: The reverse direction, for rejoining the group in Italy after skipping a day.
services.caveat: Departure times here are indicative only — the southbound timetable was not verified departure by departure.

source.title: FlixBus — Courmayeur to Chamonix route page

services.name: Line 581 — Aosta to Courmayeur

booking.where: Aosta bus station or a tobacconist

services.note: The Italian trunk route. Connects Courmayeur to the Milan, Turin and Malpensa coaches, and to the bus over the Grand-Saint-Bernard from Martigny.
services.caveat: Roughly hourly through the day, but the pattern was not verified departure by departure.

services.name: Arriva coach — Milan Malpensa to Aosta

booking.where: Arriva Italia commercial lines

services.note: Runs all year. The sensible way in if anyone flies into Milan rather than Geneva, or flies home from Italy after leaving the trail at Courmayeur.
services.caveat: Departure times and fare are indicative; the commercial line timetable was not verified in detail.

services.name: Line 12.272 — Orsières to Praz-de-Fort, La Fouly and Ferret

booking.where: sbb.ch, the CFF app, FAIRTIQ, or cash with the driver
booking.note: Drivers on this line will take euros as well as francs.

services.note: The Swiss Val Ferret line. Riding it out to Ferret saves the last 45 minutes into La Fouly, and riding it down to Orsières is how you skip day 5 entirely.
services.caveat: Roughly hourly is the shape, not a promise — check sbb.ch for the day you need. Swiss timetables for July 2027 are already published there.

services.name: Line 12.271 — Orsières to Champex

booking.where: sbb.ch, the CFF app, FAIRTIQ, or cash with the driver

services.note: Pair this with 12.272 and change at Orsières to skip day 5 from La Fouly to Champex-Lac. The change at Orsières is easy — same forecourt.
services.caveat: Some trail guides call this line 273. TMR's own timetable list says 12.271 is Orsières–Champex and 12.273 goes to Commeire instead.

services.name: St-Bernard Express — Orsières to Martigny

booking.where: sbb.ch, the CFF app, or station machines

services.note: Gets you from the Val Ferret side onto the Swiss main line in under half an hour.
services.caveat: Sold and timetabled as one journey, but the 2027 feed models it as an Orsières–Sembrancher shuttle joining the Martigny train at Sembrancher, so expect a short platform change. That is also why it has no gtfs block: no single feed trip covers both ends, and the twenty-five minutes here already includes the change.

services.name: Line 12.230 — Col de la Forclaz to Trient and Le Châtelard

booking.where: Cash with the driver, or in advance on sbb.ch
booking.note: Reservation required 72 hours ahead for groups of 10 or more, on +41 27 721 68 40 or voyages@tmrsa.ch.

services.note: Saves the 40-minute descent from the Forclaz down to Trient, and reaches the Mont-Blanc Express at Le Châtelard for a train back to Chamonix.
services.caveat: Daily only from 29 June to 30 August; weekends either side of that. Not every run continues past Le Châtelard to Finhaut. Times are from the 2026 timetable dated 26 May 2026. This bus is not in the Swiss annual GTFS feed — seasonal additions are published separately — so it cannot be re-derived and has no gtfs block.

source.title: TMR — Bus été 2026, Col de la Forclaz – Finhaut (line 12.230)

services.name: Line 12.230 — Le Châtelard and Trient to Col de la Forclaz

booking.where: Cash with the driver, or in advance on sbb.ch

services.note: The uphill direction, for rejoining the trail at Trient after a night down the valley or a train from Chamonix.
services.caveat: Modelled separately because the return times are not a mirror. Some runs start at Finhaut rather than Le Châtelard. Like the downhill direction, this one is absent from the Swiss annual feed and stays hand-recorded.

source.title: TMR — Bus été 2026, Col de la Forclaz – Finhaut (line 12.230)

services.name: PostBus — Col de la Forclaz to Martigny

booking.where: sbb.ch or cash with the driver

services.note: The way down to a bed in Martigny when Trient and the Forclaz are both full, which happens often — there are only four places to stay up there.
services.caveat: Weekday times only, reconstructed from a trail guide rather than an operator timetable. Saturday was reported as 16:09 and 17:45, Sunday as 16:09 alone. Verify on sbb.ch.

source.title: Tour du Mont Blanc Hike — public transport

services.name: Mont-Blanc Express — Martigny to Chamonix and Saint-Gervais

booking.where: sbb.ch, the CFF app, or station machines
booking.note: Free between Servoz and Vallorcine with a Chamonix valley Carte d'Hôte.

services.note: The spine that ties the Swiss and French sides together. This is how you get from Trient or Champex back to Chamonix without crossing a col, and how you reach Les Contamines by rail via Saint-Gervais.
services.caveat: Roughly hourly, with a change at the border on some services. The Swiss 2027 timetable is already published on sbb.ch, so this is one to re-derive from the feed rather than trust as a pattern.

services.name: Rail — Geneva Airport to Martigny

booking.where: sbb.ch or the CFF app
booking.note: Buy a supersaver ticket in advance for roughly half this fare.

services.note: The all-rail way in: land at Geneva, train along the lake to Martigny, then the Mont-Blanc Express to Chamonix. Slower than a shuttle but immune to Saturday traffic on the Chamonix road.
services.caveat: Frequency is the shape of the Swiss main line rather than a verified departure list. Re-derive from the 2027 feed.

services.name: Rail — Geneva Airport to Bourg-Saint-Maurice

booking.where: SNCF Connect, or sbb.ch for the Swiss portion
booking.note: Involves a change, usually at Bellegarde or Chambéry. Book the TGV leg early for a sensible fare.

services.note: The back door onto the trail. Worth knowing if somebody is joining partway through and wants to start at Les Chapieux rather than walk two days to catch up.
services.caveat: Departures and duration are indicative — this is a multi-leg rail journey with several possible routings, not a single service. Roughly four hours. Check SNCF Connect for the day.

services.name: Rail — Saint-Gervais-le-Fayet to Bourg-Saint-Maurice

booking.where: SNCF Connect, or the ticket desk at Le Fayet
booking.note: One ticket, but a change at Annecy or Albertville. Ask for the through fare rather than buying the legs separately.

services.note: The only scheduled way round the Beaufortain, and the leg that makes day 2 skippable at all: Les Contamines down to Le Fayet on the Y84, this train to Bourg-Saint-Maurice, then the navette up to Les Chapieux. Three hours to cover what takes a day on foot over the Col du Bonhomme, because the road goes the long way round the massif.
services.caveat: Times and fare are indicative. Like the Geneva service, this is a multi-leg journey rather than one train, and the routing varies by time of day. Check SNCF Connect. If it looks too slow to be worth it, that is the honest answer — Taxi Aarthur will do the same trip by road in about two hours.

walks.note: Road walk up the valley from the navette terminus to the refuge, where the Col de la Seigne climb starts.
Flat valley road and track. The free navette covers it if you would rather not.
Up through the woods to the col, where the hotel and the Martigny bus are.
The climb back up to the border col, if you are rejoining the walk part way through day 7.
Up the Swiss Val Ferret to the highest bus stop. About 45 minutes.

onDemand.name: Taxi Aarthur — Beaufortain and Vallée des Glaciers
onDemand.leadTime: Ring ahead, ideally the day before in July

fares.note: Via Bourg-Saint-Maurice and the Petit-Saint-Bernard or the Mont Blanc tunnel. The realistic way to skip from the French side to Courmayeur in one move.

No published price for this one — ask. About two hours by road round the Beaufortain via Albertville and Beaufort, against eight by train and bus, which is why it is worth the call if day 2 is the one somebody has to miss.

source.title: Adventure Base — Tour du Mont Blanc trek logistics

onDemand.name: Mountain Drop-offs — Geneva Airport to the Chamonix valley
onDemand.leadTime: Book online in advance; they meet the flight

fares.note: Shared shuttle, door to door, both directions available.

onDemand.name: Alpybus — Geneva Airport to Chamonix
onDemand.leadTime: Book online; shared departures are assigned around your flight time

fares.note: Express line, fixed pick-up and drop-off points. Door-to-door and private cost more.
